title: Records and the missed chance to record
summary: Robinson never recorded; musicians such as Kelly and Petit did not; Punch Miller recorded in Chicago.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I'd like to look over and see if you have any records that you'd sell.

I'd be able to use up at Tulane too. We have quite a few. I don't know. You've got pretty good eyes, y'all. Yes, if you have a candy. My eyes are so bad. Well, I think of it. Did you ever make any records yourself? Did you ever record? No, I never did. Never did record?
In those days, I guess not very many musicians down here got a chance to record.
Got a chance for it, that's right. Just years late, seeing my time coming up, I didn't get that chance.
It's too bad Chris Kelly didn't and Buddy Petit, none of those fellows made records. Punch did and Armstrong and a lot of others.
Yeah, but I think Punch only got that when he left here.
Yes, but Chicago he made it.
Yeah. Little Henry Rainey, that was a pretty good little trumpet. Well, after all that opportunity with him.
He made some in the very end when his lip wasn't as good as when he was younger, I guess. He made some about 1940, I think. But if they made him 10 or 15 years before, they would have had some.
And he was kind of old.
He played real nice though on those last ones. Yeah. Nice blues and clarinet marmalade. Oh yeah. High Society and a few of those numbers.
Yeah, he could play it. Rene would play a good little trumpet for him.
